On 9 November 2025 the Minister Delegate for Digital Economy and Innovation presented the Startup Act Djibouti bill, with a label, tax incentives, a proposed National Fund of Funds and a startup visa, to the National Assembly, which gave a favourable opinion with amendments for plenary.
Dr Houssein Ahmed Assoweh lists the Startup Act among the texts Djibouti already has, and the roadmap recommends adapting its mechanisms to AI-using firms.
La Nation, citing the UNESCO-backed readiness report, lists the Start-Up Act among Djibouti's existing foundations.
The guide says an innovative, high-growth firm can apply for the Startup label to obtain reinforced tax and social advantages.
